input: What are the treatments for Paroxysmal Hemicrania ?
output: The nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID) indomethacin often provides complete relief from symptoms. Other less effective NSAIDs, calcium-channel blocking drugs (such as verapamil), and corticosteroids may be used to treat the disorder. Patients with both paroxysmal hemicrania and trigeminal neuralgia (a condition of the 5th cranial nerve that causes sudden, severe pain typically felt on one side of the jaw or cheek) should receive treatment for each disorder.

input: What are the symptoms of Glycogen storage disease type 13 ?
output: Glycogen storage disease type 13 causes muscle pain (myalgia). Individuals with GSD13 also experience exercise intolerance, which means they have difficulty exercising because they may have muscle weakness and tire easily. Clinical findings include adult onset, autosomal recessive inheritance, elevated serum creatine phosphokinase, exercise intolerance, increased muscle glycogen content, and myalgia.

input: What are the symptoms of Type 2 Diabetes ?
output: Symptoms of type 2 diabetes often develop slowly and include increased thirst and frequent urination, increased hunger, feeling tired and fatigued, blurred vision, slow-healing sores or frequent infections, and areas of darkened skin. Some people with type 2 diabetes have no symptoms at first.
